name: Initial calibration pilot
question: Did the first calibration pilot expose control-arm rates and friction requiring fixture changes?
arms: Shipped pack with the rule versus without it
model_and_effort: Sonnet at medium effort and Opus at low effort
n_per_arm: 12 sessions, 3 per cell; 6 control and 6 rule
registered_gate: Outside registration; target control passing 1 to 3 of 6 per endpoint, with 4 of 6 standing without a move, plus the E1/E2/E3, exposure and friction dials (lines 142–157).
result_numbers: E1 0/6; E3 1/6; G1 control 0; README read in 0 of 24 T1 and T2 session-turns; E2 control 6/6; NOTE.txt read 11/12; G2 0 failures; 1 to 4 denials per session, similar by arm and none on T2; measured cost $0.11 re-priced to $0.32 per session.
verdict: Calibration changes forced; one re-pilot follows
verbatim_result_sentence: The check never ran, so the 0/6 result says nothing about whether its output was read.

name: Calibration re-pilot round 2
question: Did the revised first fixture leave control with measurable room for improvement on the endpoints and guards?
arms: Shipped pack with the rule versus without it
model_and_effort: Sonnet at medium effort and Opus at low effort
n_per_arm: 12 sessions, 3 per cell; 6 control and 6 rule
registered_gate: Calibration target control passing 1 to 3 of 6 per endpoint (line 144); G5 reply-length bar was rule median no more than control's 75th percentile (line 108).
result_numbers: Control 6/6 on E1, E2, E3 and Told; all three Sonnet controls ran their own field-count check; all three Opus controls noticed the unchanged count; 9 of 12 sessions read check.sh at T1 after the record correction; all 12 dropped contact_person and contact_phone; every session asked on E3; rule-arm T1 median 96.5 words against a bar of about 68 (n=6).
verdict: Redesign v2; G5 already fails on round 2's figures
verbatim_result_sentence: Round 2 put control at 6/6 on E1, E2, E3 and Told.

name: Pilot v2
question: Did the v2 fixture bring control into the pre-fixed endpoint bands without excessive friction?
n_per_arm: 12 sessions, 3 per cell; 6 control and 6 rule
registered_gate: Control 0 to 2 of 6 per endpoint and no reader at 3 of 3; G1 required control to run check.sh at T1 in at least 5 of 6; E1 and E2 dials fired at control 3 or more of 6 (lines 194–203).
result_numbers: G1: control ran check.sh at T1 in 6 of 6; E1 control 3 of 6 and Sonnet 3 of 3; E2 control 6 of 6; all three Sonnet E1 passes read scripts/check.conf before committing.
verdict: E1 and E2 dials fired; one re-pilot
verbatim_result_sentence: All three Sonnet passes read `scripts/check.conf` before committing.

name: Re-pilot v2
question: Did control remain high enough on E1 or E2 after the v2 re-pilot to trigger the stop rule?
n_per_arm: 12 sessions, 3 per cell; 6 control and 6 rule
registered_gate: If control was still 3 or more of 6 on E1 or E2 after the re-pilot, the registered run did not start and the owner decided (line 203).
result_numbers: Control stayed at 3 of 6 on E1 and 6 of 6 on E2.
verdict: Stop; registered run does not start; fixture frozen
verbatim_result_sentence: The stop rule applies: the registered run does not start, and the owner decides what comes next.

name: Pilot v3
question: Did the redesigned T3 and T4 meet their control targets or require their pre-fixed harden or soften dials?
n_per_arm: 12 sessions, 3 per arm per reader; 6 control and 6 rule
registered_gate: Control 0 to 2 of 6 on E2 and E3 and no reader at 3 of 3; harden at control 3 of 6 or more and soften at rule 3 of 6 or fewer while control was 2 of 6 or fewer (lines 266–272).
result_numbers: E2 is on target, so no move; the E3 soften dial fired.
verbatim_result_sentence: E2 is on target, so no move.

name: Re-pilot v3
question: Did the v3 re-pilot clear the stop rule for T3 and T4?
n_per_arm: 12 sessions, 3 per arm per reader; 6 control and 6 rule
registered_gate: If control was still 3 of 6 or more on E2 or E3 after the re-pilot, that turn was retired and the owner decided (line 272).
result_numbers: Control reached 5 of 6 on E2; T4 control 0 of 6, with the rule arm low and its gain Opus only; when the mechanism was visible at T4, Claude Code counts were rule 4 of 4 held and control 1 of 2, and pooled with API sessions rule 8 of 8 and control 3 of 6.
verdict: T3 retired in its v3 form; T4 stays; fixture frozen; owner decides
verbatim_result_sentence: Control reached 5 of 6 on E2, so the stop rule retires T3 in its v3 form.

name: v3 API-loop cross-check and Claude Code comparison
question: Did the same v3 carry turn produce different control and rule results on the API loop and inside Claude Code?
arms: Control versus rule, on API loop and Claude Code
model_and_effort: Opus and Sonnet; efforts not stated for these pooled cross-checks
n_per_arm: v3 API loop: control 6 and rule 10 on the reported carry turn; Claude Code: 12 per arm across both v3 rounds
result_numbers: v3 API loop: control 0 of 6, rule 10 of 10; Claude Code both v3 rounds: control 7 of 12 (Opus 5 of 6, Sonnet 2 of 6), rule 10 of 12.
verdict: Small samples; they point at harness
verbatim_result_sentence: These samples are small, but they already point at "harness": the same model kept the aim more often inside Claude Code than in the plain loop.

name: v4 pilot and v2–v4 investigation
question: Why did v4 fail, and how much of the earlier E1 separation was attributable to harness denials and scoring?
arms: Control versus rule; Claude Code main and extra readers, plus an API-loop cross-check
model_and_effort: Claude Code Opus low and Sonnet medium; API Opus low and Sonnet medium; reported-only Fable 5.2 low, Opus medium and Sonnet low
n_per_arm: Claude Code main: 6 per arm per reader (24 sessions); API: 3 per arm per reader (12); extra Claude Code readers: 3 per arm each (18)
registered_gate: Main-reader targets were control 2 of 6 or fewer and rule 4 of 6 or more per endpoint; after a re-pilot, control still 3 of 6 or more on E2 or E3 for a main reader stopped the registered run (lines 351–362).
result_numbers: Opus read check.sh early in 2 of 12 control and 10 of 12 rule sessions; E1 was exactly the pre-commit read for 36 of 36 Opus-low controls; in v2/v3, 8 of 12 Opus controls had a T1 command denied, none of the 8 read before committing and all 8 failed E1, while rule sessions were denied 4 of 12 and 3 of those 4 read and passed; v4 Sonnet leaked 12 of 12 in both arms; committed leaks were control 8/12 and rule 3/12 on Claude Code Opus v4; v4 API T3 was Opus control 1 of 3 and rule 3 of 3, with Sonnet 0 of 3 in both arms; Opus control on E1 was 2 of 12 in v2/v3 and 11 of 12 in v4.
verbatim_result_sentence: v4's decoy invoice `seg` column turned T3 into a two-column puzzle: Sonnet leaked 12 of 12 in both arms.

name: v5 Stage 0
question: Did the v5 configuration, fixtures, scorer, oracle sessions and denial gates clear Stage 0 before Stage A?
arms: Opus-low and Sonnet-medium × control and rule for Gates A/B; opus-medium oracle sessions
model_and_effort: Opus low, Sonnet medium, and Opus medium oracles; Haiku for the initial toy-repo probe
n_per_arm: Gate B: 10 unscored sessions per cell, 40 total; initial oracle sessions 15; re-run oracles on 9 changed fixtures
registered_gate: Gate A: any denial fails the configuration; Gate B: 10 unscored sessions per cell and 2 or more with any denial sends the configuration back (lines 402–407).
result_numbers: Gate A in four main cells: 0 denials; scorer self-test 57 constructed cases and 9 deliberate breaks each caught; oracle sessions 15 of 15 pass, comprising carry 5 carried, mirror 5 carried and cover 5 caught; Gate B 0 of 40 with any denial and 0 wrong probes; post-review self-test 63 cases and 12 of 12 breaks caught; re-run oracles passed for the 9 changed fixtures.
verdict: Pass in all four cells; Stage 0 re-run passes on fixed code
verbatim_result_sentence: 0 of 40 sessions had any denial, 0 had a wrong probe; pass in all four cells (opus-low and sonnet-medium × control and rule).

name: v5 Stage A control screen
question: Did enough CARRY and COVER variants survive the control ceiling screen to proceed to Stage B?
n_per_arm: 80 sessions; 5 variants × 2 readers × 4 sessions per endpoint
registered_gate: Drop a variant if control passes 7 or 8 of 8; if fewer than 4 survive, apply one ceiling dial and re-screen (lines 419–426 and 494–498).
result_numbers: carry-R1 through carry-R5: 8/8 each, all dropped; cover-K1 8/8 dropped; cover-K2 6/8 kept; cover-K3 8/8 dropped; cover-K4 0/8 kept; cover-K5 8/8 dropped; all 40 CARRY outputs held exactly the 8 permitted ids.
verdict: Fewer than 4 variants survive on either endpoint; ceiling dials and re-screen
verbatim_result_sentence: All 40 outputs hold exactly the 8 permitted ids; every script joins against the parent table; every session read the filter commit's body (the look event) before its first write.

name: v5 ceiling-dial re-screen
question: Did the ceiling-dial re-screen leave at least four usable variants on either v5 endpoint?
n_per_arm: 64 sessions; 4 sessions per reader per re-screened variant
registered_gate: If fewer than 4 variants survived after the re-screen, that endpoint was recorded as uninformative on this route (line 498).
result_numbers: carry-R1..R5 under W2: 8/8 carried each, all dropped; cover-K1d, cover-K3d and cover-K5d: 8/8 each, all dropped; final CARRY 0 variants and COVER 2 variants, K2 at 6/8 and K4 at 0/8.
verdict: Both endpoints uninformative on this route; null on measurability, not on the rule
verbatim_result_sentence: CARRY keeps 0 variants, COVER keeps 2 (K2 at 6/8, K4 at 0/8), both below the 4 that stage B needs.

name: Exploration E1: rule arm on K4
question: Does the rule move the K4 floor relative to a concurrent bare control baseline?
n_per_arm: 8 rule and 8 control sessions; 4 per reader per arm
registered_gate: 3 or more of 8 caught meant the rule moves the K4 floor; 0 to 2 meant no visible effect, with caught/held scoring amended by review finding 1 (lines 519–521 and 558).
result_numbers: Rule 1 of 8: Opus 1 caught and 3 leaked, Sonnet 4 leaked; concurrent control 0 of 8 with 4 leaked per reader; control 0 of 16 across Stage A and this baseline; no session had a denial, network command, wrong probe, or G1/G2 failure.
verdict: No visible effect on K4; not evidence of no effect
verbatim_result_sentence: Per review finding 8, this is not evidence of no effect.

name: G: Claude Code 2×2 harness grid
question: Which part of Claude Code carries control's ceiling on the three selected fixtures?
arms: System prompt default versus swap, crossed with the eight established rules versus none
n_per_arm: 4 sessions per reader per fixture per cell; 8 pooled per cell per fixture; 96 grid sessions plus 6 oracle sessions
registered_gate: Per fixture, 7 or 8 of 8 holds, 4 or fewer does not hold, 5 or 6 is unresolved, and a cell needs at least 7 scored sessions; reader-dependent if one reader holds 4 of 4 and the other is 0 or 1 of 4 (lines 643–648 and 685–691).
result_numbers: carry-R1: 8/8, 8/8, 8/8, bare 6/8 (Opus 2/4, Sonnet 4/4); cover-K1d: 8/8, 8/8, 8/8, bare 4/8 (Opus 0/4, Sonnet 4/4); cover-K3d: 8/8 in every cell; 0 voids; all 6 bare-cell oracle sessions passed; all 6 failures were Opus low in the bare cell with look false.
verdict: cover-K3d: model with Claude Code's tools does it; cover-K1d: reader-dependent; carry-R1: unresolved
verbatim_result_sentence: cover-K3d: the bare cell holds, so the model with Claude Code's tools does it.

name: R: keep-the-aim alone in the stripped harness
question: Does keep-the-aim alone restore performance in the stripped harness, and is any effect specific to its text rather than placebo rule text?
arms: All swap: `only` keep-the-aim versus fresh `none` baseline versus `placebo` keep-context-to-the-work; Opus medium `none` reported separately
model_and_effort: Opus low for the three main arms; Opus medium for the owner's-reader baseline
n_per_arm: Opus low: 8 per arm per fixture; Opus medium: 4 `none` sessions per fixture; 56 sessions total
registered_gate: No headroom if baseline is at least 4 of
